chunks: And it will be said to those who feared Allah: 'What has your Lord sent down?' They will say: 'Good.' For those who do good there is good in this world, but certainly the abode of the Hereafter is better. And how excellent the home of the righteous!
ai.seo_question: What did the pious say when asked what their Lord sent down?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to demonstrate the immediate, intuitive response of the pious, who prioritize the eternal reward of the Hereafter over worldly gains, reflecting the concept of 'Hasanah' as both worldly peace and ultimate bliss. The phrase 'Dar al-Muttaqin' (the dwelling of the pious) is interpreted not merely as Paradise but as the spiritual state of closeness to God achieved through taqwa, a theme central to Imam Ali's teachings in Nahj al-Balagha. This affirmation underscores the Quran as the source of this 'good,' linking divine revelation directly to the quality of the believer's final abode.
